title: Memorize, Adapt, Ignore: Diagnosing Robot Learning Mechanisms under Training Data Variation
models: ACT policies (peg insertion; real cube pick-and-place)
action_head: mixed: regression heads (CNN, ACT, OpenVLA-OFT), discrete action tokens (OpenVLA); no flow-matching VLA studied
methods: empirical neural tangent kernel (eNTK), restricted to LoRA adapters for large models
kernel effective rank and block structure (memorize vs adapt regimes)
Factor Sensitivity Ratio / SNR: mean kernel distance for task-relevant vs nuisance factor changes on matched probe pairs
CKA of kernel with factor label kernels
comparison with last-hidden-layer and output kernels
question: Can representation kernels tell whether a policy memorizes, adapts to, or ignores a factor of training-data variation, and predict OOD robustness or shortcut learning without rollouts?
key_findings: Toy and RL settings: with few randomized colors the eNTK is block-structured (memorize regime); with more colors it flattens (adapt) and nuisance variation collapses (ignore); the OOD success jump coincides with the effective-rank turnover, while in-distribution success is near perfect throughout.
ManiSkill RL: kernel cosine similarity correlates with success on unseen colors (Spearman rho 0.57-0.92 across four training settings, p <= 0.0019).

ACT peg insertion: the no-variation policy has the lowest validation loss but the worst OOD success; eNTK SNR tracks OOD success from 0.05 to 0.43, and joint-probe SNR orders four training-composition conditions by joint OOD success.
VLAs: lighting SNR ranks OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT and RIPT-VLA in the same order as their LIBERO-plus lighting robustness, with OpenVLA most lighting-sensitive (three models).

Shortcut detection in OpenVLA-OFT (RoboTwin): when a third task breaks a scene-language confound, the scene-to-language FSR falls and is lower than a continued-training control (which stays at 15.0) at all 10 step-matched checkpoints; eNTK and last-hidden kernels detect this (p = 0.002), the output kernel does not (4/10, p = 0.16).
Independent vs confounded variation at equal budget (RoboTwin place-object-scale): lower action error on novel categories (0.0755 vs 0.0846) with similar in-distribution error (0.0587 vs 0.0605).
Hardware ACT cube task: lightness randomization raises training SNR from 2.5 to 5.5, and success rises from 1/10 to 8/10 (bright), 1/10 to 6/10 (dark), 6/10 to 10/10 (in-distribution).

evidence.setting: both (simulation: ManiSkill, LIBERO, RoboTwin; real robot ACT study)
benchmarks: RoboTwin 2.0 (adjust bottle, shake bottle, place object on scale)
evidence.scale: toy: 10 color subsets per Ncolor; VLA model ranking over 3 models; shortcut study 10 step-matched checkpoints and 80 grasp-frame probes; hardware 10 trials per condition
evidence.statistics: partial: Spearman correlations with p-values, sign-test style p-values across checkpoints, mean +/- SD for some SNRs; no CIs on success rates
evidence.baselines: validation loss as a robustness proxy; last-hidden and output kernels as alternative diagnostics; confounded vs independent data design

causal_validation: Indirect: the causal manipulations are of training data (which factors vary), and kernel statistics are shown to track the resulting OOD behavior. No interventions on model internals.
closed_loop: OOD success numbers are closed-loop (simulation and hardware); the kernel diagnostics themselves are computed on static probe sets without rollouts, which is the point of the method. The VLA data-composition result uses offline action error.
limitations_stated: Requires probe sets built around known factors, so it cannot discover unknown sources of variation.
Kernel metric magnitudes are not comparable across kernel types; conclusions rest on within-kernel trends.
critique: The VLA evidence is thin: model ranking is a 3-model ordering match, and the shortcut study is one task family on OpenVLA-OFT; the strongest quantitative support comes from small CNN/ACT policies.
No flow-matching or diffusion-head VLA is analyzed, so whether eNTK-on-LoRA diagnostics behave the same for pi0-style action experts is open.
Useful methodological point for the review: output-space and last-hidden kernels have complementary blind spots, and validation loss can rank policies opposite to OOD robustness.

Connects to the 'memorized trajectory family' findings (2609.39971, 2604.18000): confounded training data yields memorize-like geometry, and breaking confounds shifts representations toward the task-relevant factor.
one_line: Empirical NTK statistics on matched probe sets distinguish policies that memorize, adapt to, or ignore a factor of training-data variation and track OOD robustness and visual shortcut learning, demonstrated mostly on small policies and briefly on OpenVLA-family models.
